headline: A SpaceX share for every kid in America, Musk says.
summary: Elon Musk posted on X before 4 a.m. Monday that next year he will give one SpaceX share to "every kid in America." A share closed Friday at $146.03. The US has about 73 million children under 18, so the pledge comes to about $10.66 billion. He gave no detail on how, or on who counts as a kid. He called it "the first of many."

cover_question.q: Is $10 billion a lot for Musk?

cover_answer: Hardly. He holds billions of shares. This is one each.
table_question: Is a gift still a gift if it costs the giver almost nothing?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A very rich man, Elon Musk, says next year he will give every kid in America one tiny piece of his rocket company. A company is cut into pieces called shares, like a pizza cut into millions of slices. One slice costs about $146 today. He hasn't said how yet, and that's fine.
5-7.why: A rich man, a pizza, one slice. A six-year-old takes one vivid thing for the whole story, so the slice is the story and the $10 billion stays out.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them and takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script hands them a pizza and one slice and leaves the $10 billion out. Expect "when do I get it?" The honest answer: he said next year, and he has not said how. Nothing to wait by the door for.

8-12.script: Sunday, the AI company Anthropic said it would put 5% of its shares in a public fund. Musk replied: give them straight to the public. By 4 a.m. Monday he had posted his own offer: one SpaceX share, about $146, for each of America's 73 million kids. A coupon with no store named on it.
8-12.why: Post, reply, counter-offer. The coupon is the open link.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect and whether grown-ups keep their word, so the script runs the chain in order: Anthropic's fund, Musk's reply, his own offer by 4 a.m., the price tag. The coupon with no store is the open link. Expect "so is it real?" He posted it. No one has said how a kid collects.

13-17.script: Is $10.6 billion a lot for Musk? He holds billions of SpaceX shares, so one each for 73 million kids is a small dent. Second: it came a day after Anthropic put 5% of its shares into a public fund. His reply: "give the shares directly to the public." He has given $276 million to the midterms since July.
13-17.why: Big number first, then what it costs him. Teens want both.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: $10.6 billion is a real sum, and it is a small dent for a man who owns billions of shares. The script gives both figures and the timing beside Anthropic's fund, then lets them weigh it. Expect "why does he want to?" The articles don't say. Say so, and ask what they would guess.

5-7.a: No. A tiny piece of the company that builds them, on paper. He hasn't said how yet.

8-12.a: One slice of a company. SpaceX is cut into billions. One slice: $146.03 on Friday.
He says next year. He hasn't said how, or whether every kid counts.

13-17.q: Is $10 billion a lot for Musk?
13-17.a: Hardly. He owns billions of SpaceX shares. One each is a small dent.

13-17.q: Why the day after Anthropic's fund?
13-17.a: He told them to give shares straight to the public, then said he would.
